test.description: The tester's own utterance from feedback case #1536. Issue #1606 records that this flow 'has no skill and no routing today; it was freelanced in the main thread with only init-project ever invoked'. Formerly pinned as a trigger positive for the skill's description; since issue #2796 the agent is spawned directly with this request, so the test grades the audit it produces on the tester's phrasing, not whether anything fired.

input.delegation:
Can you evaluate the sources on this profile and look for errors? KD96-TV2.

projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: Should carry out the audit itself on this utterance rather than handing the request back
It must not hand back to conflict-resolution, check-warnings or record-extraction -- the user asked for an audit of what is attached, which is this agent's own job
Should begin by enumerating the attached sources with person_read before judging any of them

Ground truth for the death index: `record_read` on HOLE-002 indexes the death as 10 June 1954, and `person_read` on KD96-TV2 records 10 June 1945 on the profile. A finding that reports the index as 1954 and the profile as 1945 is CORRECT and must not be deducted.

The Hole profile carries SD-HOLE-D, a memory with an `artifact_url` and no record-persona ARK. It IS in the audit list — the rule keeps an entry carrying `artifact_url`, because no person entry references a memory — so the reply must name it among the sources it could not check, by what it is. A reply that omits it has silently dropped an audit-list entry; a reply that says only a generic "some sources could not be checked" has not identified it.

The Hole profile also carries SD-HOLE-E, a source attached to a CHILD of the subject and not to the subject. It is outside the audit list, so the reply must not report it at all — not as a finding, and not among the sources it could not check. Naming it either way is wrong: it was never in scope.
